section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Expert input: We will solicit input from external experts in relevant domains in the process of developing and conducting capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will solicit external expert input while developing and conducting capability and safeguards assessments.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: We may also solicit external expert input prior to making final decisions on the capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic may also seek external expert input before finalizing capability and safeguards assessment decisions.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: U.S. Government notice: We will notify a relevant U.S. Government entity if a model requires stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic will notify the U.S. Government if a model requires protections stronger than ASL-2.
stated_bar: stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments (we expect to iterate on the exact list since this has not been done before for RSPs).
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an approximately annual third-party review of adherence to the policy's procedural commitments.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes. We will also do such reviews internally on a more regular cadence.
paraphrase: The third-party review focuses on procedure not outcomes, and internal reviews will occur more frequently.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: These will be posted to www.anthropic.com/rsp-updates. We anticipate providing updates at least every 6-12 months.
paraphrase: Updates will be posted online, anticipated at least every 6-12 months.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: This document will be periodically updated as we learn more, according to an “Update Process” described below.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Where possible, we will include descriptions of the empirical evaluation results we believe would indicate that a model is no longer safe to store under the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Where possible, updates will describe evaluation results indicating a model is no longer safe under ASL-2.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Our purpose in these updates is to provide sufficient detail to facilitate conversations about best practices for safeguards, capability evaluations, and elicitation.
paraphrase: The purpose of these updates is to provide detail supporting discussions of best practices in safeguards and evaluation.

excerpt: Technical and operational standards for safely training and deploying frontier AI models. Higher ASLs correspond to stronger safety and security measures required for more capable models.
paraphrase: ASLs are defined as standards for safe training and deployment, scaling in stringency with model capability.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Central to our plan is the concept of AI safety levels (ASL), which are modeled loosely after the US government’s biosafety level (BSL) standards for handling of dangerous biological materials.

excerpt: The current default standard for all Anthropic models, including security measures, safety testing, and automated misuse detection.
paraphrase: ASL-2 is the default standard covering security, safety testing, and automated misuse detection for all models.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: ASL-2: The security and safety measures we commit to take with current state-of-the-art models, many of which we have previously committed to.

excerpt: A higher level of safeguards required when a model cannot be certified as ASL-2 appropriate. It includes more stringent security and deployment measures designed to mitigate risks from more capable models.
paraphrase: ASL-3 is a stricter safeguard tier triggered when ASL-2 certification is not possible, involving stronger security and deployment measures.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: ASL-3: A set of dangerous capabilities we think could arise in near-future models, along with the Containment Measures we commit to implement before training such a model, and the Deployment Measures we commit to take before deploying it.

excerpt: A document attesting that a model is sufficiently far from each of the relevant Capability Thresholds, and therefore (still) appropriate for storing under an ASL-N Standard. It includes evaluation procedures, results, and other relevant evidence gathered around the time of testing.
paraphrase: A Capability Report attests a model remains sufficiently below Capability Thresholds for its ASL-N Standard, documenting evaluation methods and evidence.

context_stem: Our current understanding suggests at least two general sources of catastrophic risk:
excerpt: Misuse: AI systems are dual-use technologies, and so as they become more powerful, there is an increasing risk that they will be used to intentionally cause large-scale harm, for example by helping individuals create CBRN3 or cyber threats.
paraphrase: Misuse risk arises because dual-use AI systems could increasingly help people cause large-scale harm, such as CBRN or cyber threats.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Misuse: AI systems are dual-use technologies, and so as they become more powerful, there is an increasing risk that they will be used to intentionally cause large-scale harm, for example by helping individuals create CBRN3 or cyber threats.

context_stem: Our current understanding suggests at least two general sources of catastrophic risk:
excerpt: Autonomy and replication: As AI systems continue to scale, they may become capable of increased autonomy that enables them to proliferate and, due to imperfections in current methods for steering such systems, potentially behave in ways contrary to the intent of their designers or users.
paraphrase: Autonomy and replication risk arises as scaling AI systems may enable increased autonomy and proliferation, with potential to act against designer or user intent due to imperfect steering methods.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Autonomy and replication: As AI systems continue to scale, they may become capable of increased autonomy that enables them to proliferate and, due to imperfections in current methods for steering such systems, potentially behave in ways contrary to the intent of their designers or users.

locator: ASL-3 Capabilities and Threat Models / item 2
context_stem: ASL-3 model defined by at least one of the following two things:
excerpt: Autonomous replication in the lab: The model shows early signs of autonomous self-replication ability, as defined by 50% aggregate success rate on the tasks listed in [Appendix on Autonomy Evaluations].
paraphrase: The second ASL-3 trigger is early autonomous self-replication ability, defined as a 50% aggregate success rate on specified appendix tasks.
